app.title: Single-choice text labelling (Potato radio-selection task)
app.summary: An annotator registers or signs in, then gets the text items one at a time. For each item they choose exactly one label from a fixed list, by clicking or pressing its number key, and move on to the next. Each answer is saved to the annotator's record and counted against the item. The collected labels are written out as a TSV file, and the admin pages report progress and agreement between annotators.

task.text: Give each text item exactly one category from a fixed list, so the labels can be collected, compared across annotators and exported as a dataset.

data.text: A collection of short text items loaded from a data file with an id and a text field, a fixed set of category labels, and the label each annotator gives each item.
data.item: a short text with an id

stage.text: labelling a text collection against a fixed category set, before the labels are used to train or evaluate

mechanism.text: After sign-in, a review queue shows one item's text above a single-choice radio group with number-key shortcuts, and saving an answer moves on to the next item. Saved answers are counted per item, and the admin dashboard summarises progress and agreement.

field.text: single-label text classification for building NLP datasets

workflow.name: apply one label from a fixed set to each item in a queue

steps.here: the config names a JSON data file and which keys hold each item's id and text; any user may register with a username and password

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: the annotation page shows one item's text with the question, and saving moves on to the next item

steps.step: apply one label from a fixed set to each item
steps.here: a radio group of five labels, each with a sequential number-key shortcut, so only one answer per item is allowed

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: each save registers the annotator on the item, and the admin dashboard counts annotators, items and completion
agreement between annotators is measured with Cohen's kappa for each pair of annotators and Fleiss' kappa across all of them
annotations are written to the output directory in TSV format

distinctive: the whole interface is declared in a YAML config: the label list, the question, the data keys and the export format, with no interface code to write
labels get number-key shortcuts in order, so a single choice can be made from the keyboard alone
an answer counts only once the item records its annotator, which is what drives progress, caps and agreement
the agreement report computes chance-corrected kappa, both for each pair of annotators and across all of them

parts.title: Task configuration
parts.summary: Declares the data file, the item id and text keys, the single-choice question and its labels, the key bindings and the TSV export format.

parts.title: Sign in / Register
parts.summary: Lets an annotator create an account or sign in before they reach the items, so each answer is tied to a person.

parts.title: Annotation page
parts.summary: Shows one item's text with the question and its answer choices, and moves on to the next item after each save.

parts.title: Single-choice label group
parts.summary: A radio group of the configured labels with sequential number-key shortcuts, so each item gets exactly one label.

parts.title: Answer save
parts.summary: Saves the annotator's label and records them on the item, so progress and agreement count it.

parts.title: Admin dashboard
parts.summary: Gives the person running the task counts of annotators, items and completion, along with agreement scores for the labels.

parts.summary: Computes Cohen's kappa for each pair of annotators and Fleiss' kappa across all of them, and puts each score into words.
